text.p: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in Telefonos de Mexico eased on Monday amid concerns over U.S. certification of Mexico as an ally in the fight against illicit drugs.
Most ADRs, and Latin American ones in particular, were mixed to lower in quiet trade ahead of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's congresssional testimony on the economy on Wednesday.
"I don't think you're going to see a whole lot of buying in the next couple of days," a trader in Latin American ADRs said.

Mexican bellwether Telmex was off 1/2 to 38-3/8 in moderate early-afternoon trade and was the most-active ADR. Mexico City stocks opened down on a weaker peso, rising interest rates and fears that President Bill Clinton's certification of Mexico may not be ratified by Congress.

Among other Mexican ADRs, media conglomerate Grupo Televisa was off 5/8, pulled lower in part by a Mexican newspaper report chairman Emilio Azcarraga Milmo might step down on Tuesday because of ailing health.
Oil stocks were hit by a drop in crude oil prices, with British Petroleum off 7/8 to 131-1/2 and Royal Dutch Petroleum Co falling 1-1/8 to 171-7/8.

Israel's Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd fell 9/16 to 61-1/4 after it announced it had received tentative approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for pain-fighting ketorolac tromethamine tablets.
Decliners led advancers 307 to 190 among 807 ADRs. Volume was 34.3 million shares in early afternoon.
